note: Working name (Q33). The small alphabet of A. W. N. Pugin, Glossary of Ecclesiastical Ornament (1844), plate 9 ('Alphabets No. 1'; the book's Plate X), which Pugin dates to the latter part of the fifteenth century. A textura minuscule written with a broad nib, every letter drawn with hairline flourishes. Plain forms are built from the same nib strokes and are the defaults; Pugin's flourished forms are alternates (decision 0008, decision 0011, brief 2026-10-28-textura-start).
zone_note: the lowercase rows on the flattened plate, inside the frame and below the capitals
body_note: an opening this wide removes the hairlines (about 7 px) and keeps the nib's strokes (38 px and more): what is left is each letter's body
glyphs_note: Each box (flattened-plate pixels) holds the centre of the letter's larger body pieces, which seed it; every other piece of ink, hairlines and swashes included, goes to the letter it is joined to by the shortest way along the ink. The ampersand is hairline only: the middle of its box seeds it.

spacing.note: As the Lombardic's (tools/type/spacing.py), over the x-height, but with the target white set so two i's stand one minim's pitch apart (the pitch of n's stems): a textura is spaced like a fence. The pairs still off are kerned; nothing may come closer than the clearance over the whole height, ascenders and descenders included. Provisional.
spacing.target_white_note: units, held at the value set by two i's one minim's pitch apart until 2026-10-29. That measure takes the i's whole ink, spurs and mark included, so giving the i a lighter head, a top spur and a new mark would have respaced every letter (to 60.0; measured on the i without spurs, 64.7). Held, the other letters keep their spacing.
spacing.clearance_note: units, between heads, feet and stems in the x-height band, which in a textura this tight all but touch
spacing.clearance_top_spur_note: units: how close the top spur leading into a first head (i, j, n, m, r) may come to the letter before; the letters are spaced without it. Josh, 2026-10-29, choosing from 10, 4 and touching: "4 units clear looks good"
spacing.clearance_outside_note: units, above the x-height and below the baseline: at 10, d's arm leaning back over its bowl read as touching a preceding l's or h's spur at text size

held.nib_angle_note: degrees, held rather than fitted: the nib at the heads (at the x-height line and above) and at the feet (at the baseline and below), the pen turning evenly between. Josh: "the nib angle is too shallow - needs to be a few degrees more vertical" (2026-10-29): the fit had settled at 40°, and one angle was held at 45°, the mean measured from the edges of Pugin's heads and feet (measurements.json). Then "we need to push the standard nib angle to 50 degrees. We're still too shallow", and: "There is nib rotation going on in Pugin's original. The top connecting spurs are at 45°, but the feet are nearly all at 50°" (2026-10-29).
held.nib_light_note: share of the nib's full width in a stroke written with less pressure: c's top, e's arm, the a's top bowl. Josh: "I think we need to introduce a narrower nib - perhaps for Pugin the was accomplished with less pressure? But take the top stroke of the c, for example - it should be about 20% thinner. Same with the e and top bowl on the a." (2026-10-29)
held.top_leave_note: degrees: the angle at which the concave top of c, d, e, g and s leaves the stem's top corner, before steepening to the nib's angle at the peak. Measured on the plate (c 13, d 24, e 19, g 4, s 13; their peaks are met at 39-52°); the median is held. Josh: "notice in Pugin's, the top of the c, d, e, g, and s all have a concave curve on the top left where the primary stem and top line intersect. We need to retain this. It's one of many fine features accomplished by subtle nib rotation." (2026-10-29)
held.fork_note: the split top of b, d, h, k and l (textura_letters.split_top): its notch's depth, where its horns leave the stem, how far its tips stand out, their radius (px), and how far from upright its horns run into their tips (degrees). Held, not fitted, so every ascender has the same top. Josh: "we need to make the simple split top for the b, d, h, k, and l. This is known convention in blackletter type. Pugin turns them highly decorative, which we will ultimately support through dynamic alternatives, but for now, we need a simple, clean split top that is consistent between the characters I listed, each spilt coming to a gentle rounded tip." (2026-10-29)

spur.note: plate px: the hairline a free foot carries on into, up and to the right along the nib's own edge as the pen holds it at the foot (50°), so it is exactly the nib's hairline. Pugin's are mostly 5-12 px (l's runs to about 30, tapering); set, not fitted. At 22 px and 41° they were too pronounced (Josh, 2026-10-29). On by default; the stylistic set ss01 drops them (Josh: "it would be cool to have a setting for the spur, where it can be turned on or off").

held_by_hand_note: family settings set by hand in the stroke editor on the proof page (decision 0012); last saved 2026-10-29 10:50
